To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in order to achieve a given target outage probability, the number of antennas at the transmitter and the receiver can be much lower than that of the conventional MIMO systems with a large number of antennas.
the required number of transmit/receive antennas in a large but finite MIMO system can be determined by outage probability and the number of transmit/receiver antennas.

in the outage-limited scenario, the required number(s) of the transmit/receiver antennas to satisfy a specific outage probability constraint can be obtained for different fading environments and the number(s) can be significantly smaller than the corresponding infinite MIMO case.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the required number of the antennas to satisfy different outage requirements.
a practical MIMO system in which the numbers of the transmit and receive antennas are large but finite.
the performance evaluation of a MIMO communication system with a large number of antennas at both the transmitter and receiver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a point-to-point MIMO system, the number of transmit and receive antennas required to achieve a target outage probability can be significantly reduced if the antennas at each end are correlated.
for a given outage requirement the required number of transmit and receive antennas can be significantly reduced by increasing the number of antennas.

the required number of transmit/receive antennas in the point-to-point MIMO systems with a large number of antennas is significantly smaller than the required number of the antennas in the point to point MIMO systems with the same outage probability constraint but with a finite number of transmit/receiver antennas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the outage-limited scenario, the required number (N) of antennas in a MIMO system is independent of the channel conditions, i.e. N
the required number of the antennas is not very sensitive to the outage probability constraints, the spatial correlation between antennas and the fading conditions.
in the case of the outage-limited scenario, a point-to-point MIMO system can be implemented using a relatively small number of antennas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the required numbers of antennas for a large but finite MIMO systems are significantly less than the numbers of antennas required in the infinite MIMO systems.
the outage probability of the point-to- point MIMO systems can be improved by increasing the number of antennas at the transmitter and/or the receiver.

the required number of transmit and receive antennas are independent of the number of transmit antennas at the transmitter, and are only a function of the number of receive antennas and the channel fading condition.
